niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: The Ghost Green Illusion
ideas.angle: An interactive optical test where the viewer stares at a specific point to force their brain to generate a color that isn't on the screen. It triggers massive comments because viewers want to report if it worked for them.
ideas.reason: Interactive illusions have extremely high VVSA because they give a direct command. The Troxler Effect and negative afterimages consistently go viral as they provide a 'physical' sensation of the brain glitching.

ideas.title: The Secret Body Language of Feet
ideas.angle: A social decoding hack revealing that feet point toward the person we are most interested in or away when we want to leave. Viewers will immediately test this in their next conversation, driving high shares.
ideas.reason: Social survival and 'reading minds' are high-velocity topics. This specific micro-behavior is less known than eye contact, making it feel like a 'forbidden' secret.
sources: The Dictionary of Body Language by Joe Navarro

ideas.title: The Finger Velocity Glitch
ideas.angle: An interactive physical challenge where viewers waggle their fingers in front of a TV or LED light to see a 'stroboscopic' effect. It forces a 100% completion rate as they try it while watching.
ideas.reason: Interactive physical hacks have the highest retention (APV) because the viewer is physically engaged with the screen. This exploit of the 'Persistence of Vision' is a reliable viral trigger.
sources: Stroboscopic Effect in LED lighting research
